spec.name: Upgrade Time
spec.description: Time it takes to research this upgrade. It uses the same unit as Cost: Build Time in the UDTA section: the game doubles both, and the building's progress goes up by one each step until it reaches that. Every field in this section has one entry per upgrade, 52 in all: 0 Swords 1, 1 Swords 2, 2 Axes 1, 3 Axes 2 (these four at the Blacksmiths), 4 Arrows 1, 5 Arrows 2, 6 Throwing Axes 1, 7 Throwing Axes 2 (Lumber Mills), 8 and 9 Human Shields 1 and 2, 10 and 11 Orc Shields 1 and 2 (Blacksmiths), 12 and 13 Human Ship Cannons 1 and 2, 14 and 15 Orc Ship Cannons 1 and 2, 16 and 17 Human Ship Armor 1 and 2, 18 and 19 Orc Ship Armor 1 and 2 (Foundries), 20 and 21 Catapults 1 and 2, 22 and 23 Ballistas 1 and 2 (Blacksmiths), 24 Elven Ranger Training, 25 Longbow, 26 Ranger Scouting, 27 Ranger Marksmanship, 28 Troll Berserker Training, 29 Lighter Axes, 30 Berserker Scouting, 31 Berserker Regeneration (Lumber Mills), 32 Ogres to Ogre Mages, 33 Knights to Paladins, 34 Holy Vision, 35 Healing, 36 Exorcism, 37 Flame Shield, 38 Fireball, 39 Slow, 40 Invisibility, 41 Polymorph, 42 Blizzard, 43 Eye of Kilrogg, 44 Bloodlust, 45 Raise Dead, 46 Death Coil, 47 Whirlwind, 48 Haste, 49 Unholy Armor, 50 Runes, 51 Death and Decay. The game handles the entries in two ways. Entries 0 to 31 are upgrades: when one is finished, the game adds one to the player's level counter chosen by Group, and that counter is what gives the bonus. Entries 32 to 51 are spells (and the Paladin and Ogre Mage upgrades): when one is finished, its Flags are added to the spells the player knows. Which way an entry is handled is decided by the command button that starts the research, not by this data. In a PUD, the UGRD section starts with a word in front of this data (not counted in the offsets here): if it is 0, the data is read; otherwise the data is skipped and the default upgrade data is used. The data itself is 780 bytes, so the section is 782 bytes. The default data is entry 1 of MAINDAT.WAR, which has the same 780-byte layout.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 255. Entries 34 (Holy Vision), 38 (Fireball) and 43 (Eye of Kilrogg) are 0 in the default data. These three and Death Coil (46) have no research button in the game.

spec.name: Cost: Gold
spec.description: Gold it costs to research this upgrade. Unlike the costs in the UDTA section, this is the actual amount; it is not multiplied by 10. The cost is taken when the research starts and given back if it is cancelled.

spec.name: Cost: Lumber
spec.description: Lumber it costs to research this upgrade. This is the actual amount; it is not multiplied by 10.

spec.name: Cost: Oil
spec.description: Oil it costs to research this upgrade. This is the actual amount; it is not multiplied by 10. Only the ship cannon upgrades (12 to 15) cost oil in the default data.

spec.name: Icon
spec.description: Icon shown in the panel of the selected building while it is researching this upgrade. The research button itself has its own icon in the command data of WAR2.EXE, so this does not change the button.
spec.values: Icon number, the same numbering as the icons of units and command buttons. For example 6 and 7 are the Ranger and Berserker, 10 and 11 the Paladin and Ogre Mage.

spec.name: Group
spec.description: Only used by upgrades 0 to 31: the level counter that goes up by one for the player when the upgrade is finished. Each counter is shared by all upgrades with the same group, so for example Swords 1 and 2 both use group 1, and the research buttons show level 1 or 2 depending on the counter. The bonuses themselves come from the counters, so the group decides what the upgrade does. For entries 32 to 51 the game never reads this field; in the default data it holds the number of the spell's bit in Flags.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 10 for upgrades 0 to 31. The game has only 11 counters and does not check the value, so a higher value reads past the end of its list of counters.

bits.value: Not used by any upgrade in the default data. The game reads this counter only when drawing the stats panel, so raising it has no effect on how units play.
Ranger and Berserker Training (upgrades 24 and 28). Longbow, Scouting and Marksmanship (and the Troll equivalents) can only be researched once this counter is not 0.
Ranger Marksmanship and Berserker Regeneration (upgrades 27 and 31).

spec.name: Flags
spec.description: The bit (or bits) this upgrade uses in the player's upgrade or spell bits, which are the same bits as in the ALOW section: upgrades 0 to 31 use the upgrade bits, entries 32 to 51 the spell bits. When research starts, the flags are marked as being researched for the player; when it finishes or is cancelled, the mark is removed. If the mark is already gone when the research finishes, nothing happens (no level and no refund). For upgrades 0 to 31 the flags give nothing by themselves (the bonus comes from Group). The research buttons are hidden while the bit they check is being researched, but each button checks a fixed bit, not this field; in the default data upgrade 5 (Arrows 2) has 0x01 instead of 0x02, so Arrows 2 can be started in a second Lumber Mill while the first is still researching it, and the second one to finish has no effect and its cost is lost. For entries 32 to 51 the flags are added to the spells the player knows when the research finishes; a spell's cast button is only shown when its bit is known. Two values do more when the research finishes, and only when the flags are exactly that value: 0x10000 turns all the player's Archers into Rangers and Axe Throwers into Berserkers (also those being trained), and 0x100000 turns Knights into Paladins and Ogres into Ogre Mages (also those being trained) and gives the player Holy Vision and Eye of Kilrogg if those spells are allowed.
